title: Normalized native pro-etale restriction is braided closed monoidal
statement: Let $A$ be a Grothendieck abelian symmetric closed monoidal category with additive tensor and functorial flat resolutions [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Suppose pro-etale inverse images preserve flat objects. Let $j:W\to Y$ be weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $r=D(j^*)$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories of native $A$-valued sheaves. Let $e:rK\otimes^L rL\cong r(K\otimes^L L)$ be natural and normalized by the exact-functor factorization and the ordinary homotopy oplax tensor square. Then $r$ admits a strong monoidal structure with tensor map exactly $e$. It preserves the descended Koszul braiding, and its closed comparison $rR\mathcal Hom(K,-)\to R\mathcal Hom(rK,r(-))$ is an invertible natural transformation for every $K$. No dualizing object is chosen.

source.place: Tag 08JB, lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U, with the native constant-coefficient slice construction; tensor derivation and Koszul interchange as in Tags 06YU and 0FPT.

proof.text: Identify the pro-etale site of W with the slice of Y at its weakly etale object j. Restriction is exact and strong symmetric monoidal, and its exact sum-extension left adjoint implies preservation of K-injectives. The native constant-coefficient functor upperStar is this restriction.

Use functorial K-flat resolutions to derive the ordinary tensor structure, including its unit and associativity. The Koszul interchange on complexes descends to the stated braided identity. On a pair of K-flat resolutions whose restrictions are K-flat, the maps in the normalization square are invertible, hence the square fixes the tensor component. Naturality and essential surjectivity extend this identification to all objects. Thus the tensor map is exactly e.hom.

Represent the second argument by a K-injective complex. Its restriction is K-injective. On each object of the localized site the enriched Hom complex and its differential are unchanged. Its evaluation is the same application map, so this isomorphism equals the closed comparison attached to the tensor structure, rather than merely an arbitrary isomorphism with the same endpoints. It is natural in the second variable and hence its natural transformation is invertible. The construction is unbounded and also applies to the empty site.

theorem exists_normalizedRestrictionMonoidalClosed
    (A : Type z) [Category.{u + 1} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} A] [MonoidalCategory A] [MonoidalPreadditive A]
    [SymmetricCategory A] [MonoidalClosed A] [Abelian.HasFunctorialFlatResolution A]
    [UpperStarPreservesFlat A] {W Y : Scheme.{u}} (j : W ⟶ Y) [WeaklyEtale j]
    (e : DeltaRestrictionTensorComparison A j)
    (he : IsNormalizedDeltaRestrictionTensor A j e) :
    letI := _root_.DerivedCategory.braidedCategory' (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) A)
    letI := _root_.DerivedCategory.braidedCategory' (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) A)
    ∃ m : (upperStar A j).mapDerivedCategory.Monoidal,
      letI := m
      (∀ K L, Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ (upperStar A j).mapDerivedCategory K L =
        (e.hom.app K).app L) ∧
      (∀ K L, Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ (upperStar A j).mapDerivedCategory K L ≫
          (upperStar A j).mapDerivedCategory.map (β_ K L).hom =
        (β_ ((upperStar A j).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
          ((upperStar A j).mapDerivedCategory.obj L)).hom ≫
            Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ (upperStar A j).mapDerivedCategory L K) ∧
      (∀ K, IsIso (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ihomComparison
        (upperStar A j).mapDerivedCategory K).natTrans)
